content.text:
Investigation complete. Findings:

- The document is a securitization **Transfer and Servicing Agreement**, not a supply/procurement contract — there is no purchasing relationship to make exclusive.
- Every instance of "exclusive" is unrelated: **exclusive control** over the Cap Collateral Account (p0387–p0388, a secured-party control mechanic that runs *in favor of* the Issuer, our party) and **nonexclusive** jurisdiction (p0427, which preserves rather than restricts forum options).
- Regex searches for "sole supplier", "sole and exclusive provider", "all of its requirements", "shall not procure", "exclusivity", "sole source", and compete/third-party-provider restrictions returned nothing relevant.
- No covenant anywhere restricts Verizon Owner Trust 2020-A or Verizon ABS LLC from engaging third-party providers. Section 9.2's transfer/lien restriction on the Depositor is an asset-conveyance protection for the Issuer, not a dealing exclusivity.

This satisfies the **preferred** position (no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer), so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: The Issuer agrees that it shall not assert exclusive control over, or originate entitlement orders or instructions for the disposition of funds with respect to, the Cap Collateral Account unless the conditions for the exercise of its rights and remedies pursuant to the Cap Agreement are met
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on our party, which meets the preferred position. This is a Transfer and Servicing Agreement for a securitization rather than a supply or procurement contract, so there is no purchasing relationship capable of being made exclusive. The only uses of "exclusive" are unrelated to dealing exclusivity: (i) "exclusive control" over the Cap Collateral Account in Section 9.10 (p0387-p0388), a standard secured-party account-control mechanic that operates in favor of the Issuer, and (ii) the "nonexclusive jurisdiction" submission in Section 10.6 (p0427), which preserves rather than restricts forum choice. Targeted searches for "sole supplier", "sole and exclusive provider", "all of its requirements", "shall not procure", "exclusivity", "sole source", and compete / third-party-provider restrictions returned no purchasing covenant binding the Issuer or the Depositor. Section 9.2's restriction on the Depositor transferring or encumbering the Depositor Transferred Property is an asset-conveyance protection benefiting the Issuer, not a restrictive covenant on our freedom to contract with other providers. No redline required.
